human_tolerance.notes: One of the few parrot species to have successfully adapted to living in disturbed habitats; feral populations have colonised a number of cities around the world and regularly visit gardens and bird feeders near human habitation.

phases.name: mating
phases.note: Described for the native north-western Indian population: pairs form from September to December and select and defend nest sites during this cooler season, avoiding competition with other cavity-nesters. UK-specific pairing dates were not found in an open source; this window is used as the best-sourced approximation.

phases.name: young
phases.note: Native Indian population: young are cared for from April to June and fledglings leave the nest before the monsoon.

vocalizations.description: A loud, harsh, unmistakable screeching squawk given in alarm or when disturbed, often while taking flight.

Loud, raucous, repeated screeching calls given in flight and from perches, especially as flocks gather and fly to communal roosts at dusk and disperse at dawn; winter roosts in Great Britain have held around 6,000 birds.

external.note: NCBI taxon id (P685), eBird code (P3444) and iNaturalist taxon id (P3151) via Wikidata.

range.note: Native range derived from the Distribution section's description: 'a narrow belt across the full width of the continent between about 4 to 17 N latitude' (the Sahelian belt from Senegal to Ethiopia/Eritrea, plus the Nile Valley in Egypt per the Diet section) and 'the Indian subcontinent and Sri Lanka from 6 to 35 N latitude in the foothills of the Himalaya, and from the Indus River valley in Pakistan east to the Irrawaddy River valley in Myanmar' (Pakistan, India, Nepal, Bangladesh, Myanmar, Sri Lanka). Introduced range limited to the countries the Feral Birds section states it has 'established itself on a large scale' in: Germany, France, Belgium, the Netherlands, Italy and the UK (the London/South-East England population targeted by this record is detailed in the Great Britain subsection). Many other countries with escaped or smaller feral populations (Spain, Turkey, Israel, Japan, the US, etc.) are described in the same section but omitted here as less clearly 'established'.

traits.locomotion_modes.note: Powered flight is explicit. Parrots hop on branches and the ground and climb using beak and feet; 'Climb' is not offered as a move pose by the biped_winged body plan, so only Hop and Fly are listed as locomotion modes to keep poses resolvable.

traits.nest_type.note: Nests in tree cavities (competing with, and in Europe sometimes displacing, hole-nesting bats and other cavity users per the Aggression section); also palm-tree hollows in Egypt per the Diet section.

traits.size_class.note: From mass_kg (0.12 kg falls in the Small band).

traits.mass_kg.note: Midpoint of the Asian-birds mass range, 104-143 g (rarely to 174 g), from the Description section. Feral European/British populations derive from an interbreeding mix of the Asian subspecies P. k. manillensis and P. k. borealis (per the Taxonomy section), not the smaller African birds (51-93 g), so the Asian range was used.

traits.length_m.note: Midpoint of the stated total length range, 37-43 cm, including the long tail.

traits.lifespan_y.note: Judgement: no open-licensed source with a specific lifespan figure for P. krameri was found (informal figures of ~25-30 years in captivity circulate widely but are unsourced or behind non-open sources such as IUCN/ADW, which this record avoids). 15 years is an authored estimate for a medium-bodied, non-migratory, long-lived parrot in the wild; a reviewer should replace this if a better open source turns up.

traits.diet.note: The Diet section lists 'buds, nectar, fruit, vegetables, nuts, berries, seeds, grains, and insects' with no quantified shares. Shares are an authored judgement mapping: nuts/seeds/grains and cereal grains/pigeon peas (India) to seed (dominant), fruit/berries/mulberry/dates (Egypt) to fruit, buds/vegetables to browse, nectar to nectar, and occasional insects to a small invertebrate share.

traits.social.note: Described as forming large, noisy flocks and communal winter roosts of thousands ('three separate roosts of about 6000 birds around London' in winter 2006); group_size upper bound of 50 is an authored judgement for typical day-to-day foraging flocks, well below the much larger seasonal roost aggregations noted in habitat.human_tolerance.

traits.activity_pattern.note: No explicit 'diurnal' statement, but all described foraging, flock, and roosting behaviour occurs by day with dawn/dusk roost movements; parrots generally are diurnal.

traits.defense.note: Judgement: no explicit predator-response description was found; a fast, noisy flier that flushes readily when disturbed, similar to other feral urban birds in this repository.

traits.wariness.note: Judgement: bold around people in parks and gardens where it readily takes food from bird feeders, but wary enough to flush noisily when closely approached.

habitat.use.note: Judgement: predominantly arboreal (feeds, nests and roosts in trees) with regular ground/feeder visits, informed by the Feral Birds and Diet sections.

habitat.shelter_tag.note: Roosts communally in tall trees (e.g. large winter roosts around London); 'perch' used as the closest available ResourceTag.

habitat.resources.note: Food weights follow traits.diet; cavity nesting and perch/roost shelter from the Ecology and behaviour and Aggression sections.

habitat.human_tolerance.note: Feral Birds section: escaped birds have colonised cities worldwide 'where their preferred diet... is available from suburban gardens and bird feeders'; light_max is authored judgement.

seasonal.phases.note: Timings are from the Reproduction section, which explicitly describes the native north-western Indian population, not the British feral population; no open source with UK-specific pairing/breeding dates for this species was found. Kept as the best-sourced approximation and flagged for a reviewer.

seasonal.life_stages.note: Egg, altricial juvenile and adult stages inferred from cavity nesting and fledging before the monsoon; no open source gives a juvenile duration or scale, so both were left unset rather than guessed.

vocalizations.squawk.note: 'It is a noisy species with an unmistakable squawking call' (Description section).

vocalizations.roost_call.note: Loud, raucous roost-gathering calls inferred from the description of communal winter roosts of thousands of birds around London (Great Britain subsection); time windows are an authored judgement about when flocks travel to and from roosts.

look.note: Colours from the Description section: 'a distinctive green colour in the wild with a red beak and blue tail', plus the adult male's pink and black neck ring (rendered here as a single simplified 'markings' band, since the block model has only 5 colour slots). Proportions (long tail, large head, short legs, strong hooked beak) are authored judgement typical of Psittacula parrots.

behavior.note: Authored parameters for the shared perching-songbird program. food_tag set to seed (the largest authored diet share); the program's 'song' slot is used for the loud dawn/dusk roost-gathering call rather than a melodic song, since this species has no true song. nest_m1/nest_m2 (Jan-Jun) are an authored guess bracketing nest-site selection through fledging, since only the native Indian population's Sept-Dec pairing and Apr-Jun young timing is sourced (see seasonal.phases).
